classification.difficultyReason: Decode a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot and justify an age comparison using both clustering and tail direction. The named features cue the method, but the answer must coordinate two distributions with the claim rather than give isolated shape labels.

inlines.text: The ages of members of a dance class are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot.
Pat claims that the women who attend the dance class are generally older than the men.
Is Pat correct? Justify your answer by referring to the clustering and skewness of each dataset.

spec.description: Women on the left, shared stems in the centre and men on the right. Two vertical rules enclose the stem column; one horizontal rule separates the italic headings from the data. No outer box, data-row rules, shading or printed key.
spec.mathematics: For stems 3, 4, 5, 6, women's leaves read left to right as [2], [4,2], [8,8,5,4,0,0], [9,4,3,3]; men's leaves read left to right as [4,6], [2,2,5,6,8], [3], [3]. Preserve every repeated leaf. The age context and supplied answer support interpreting stems as tens and leaves as units; this interpretation is stated in the worked answer without adding a source key.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question plot. No supplied answer or comparison statement is drawn.

answer.short: Yes. Women’s ages cluster in the 50s and 60s and are negatively skewed; men’s ages cluster in the 40s and are positively skewed.
answer.worked: Read each stem as tens and each leaf as units. The women’s ages cluster in their 50s and 60s, with a tail towards younger ages, so their distribution is negatively skewed. The men’s ages cluster in their 40s, with a tail towards older ages, so their distribution is positively skewed. The women’s cluster is at higher ages, so Pat is correct.
